recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-32439 unless a separate diagram-generation cleanup chooses to refresh source/auditevent/auditevent.svg.
issue_request: FHIR-32439 is a Published/Persuasive Security WG change request for R5. It asked that AuditEvent.type no longer be extensible, with the binding changed to example and the value set treated as example guidance for the intended event category range.
initial_application: The issue was initially applied in commit 54eab8c3547bcb192cc1158e4d08dd52a9b3db72, which changed AuditEvent.type binding strength from extensible to example. Later history, especially 87b00c9c0de977f8559e0f99694e8664e03a06cd, renamed the referenced value set and authoritative narrative links to audit-event-type-example.
additional_context: Security WG Confluence minutes and the linked Zulip block-vote thread list FHIR-32439 as Persuasive in the September 13, 2021 AuditEvent/Provenance block vote. Related FHIR-32443 drove type/category naming changes in the same family, while the current build source now exposes AuditEvent.type and maps it to Event.category. The only old audit-event-type link found in this area was in auditevent.svg, a generated-looking diagram artifact outside the authoritative XML/narrative source for this binding decision.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. The active AuditEvent resource source is in build scope, and source/auditevent/structuredefinition-AuditEvent.xml already binds AuditEvent.type with strength example to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/audit-event-type-example. The referenced value set is explicitly named and described as an example Audit Event ID/Event Categories value set.
